title: SLO Collab: Accelerant Handoff Proposal & Risk Slicing Canvas
body:
Purpose
This is a lightweight, practical proposal to accelerate cross-team SLO adoption by creating a small, repeatable 'accelerant' handoff pattern and a risk-slicing canvas that teams can use during feature launches and service onboarding. The goal is to reduce ambiguity about ownership, make trade-offs explicit, and cut the time required to reach operational acceptance from ~8 weeks to ~2-3 weeks for medium-risk services.

Audience
- Platform engineering (ownership of the handoff pattern and templates)
- Feature/product teams (service owners)
- SRE partners and on-call rotations
- Product security & compliance for gated launches

Context and motivation
We keep seeing long tails on SLO adoption: feature teams hand off services with vague SLAs, SREs spend cycles writing bespoke runbooks, and rollouts stall because risk isn't decomposed. Existing playbooks are comprehensive but heavyweight; this doc proposes a compact operational pattern (the "accelerant") that focuses on 3 concrete artifacts: 1) risk-slicing canvas, 2) ownership matrix (who is oncall/triage/maintain), 3) quick-runbook template (flipbook style).

Key principles
- Minimal viable operational acceptance: ship the smallest set of commitments and telemetry needed to be safely oncall.
- Decision anchors not endless docs: capture the trade-offs with explicit signals and thresholds.
- Iterative ramp: enable a 30/60/90 day observability and mitigation plan rather than a one-time gate.
- Make rollback/fallback the default mitigation when risk is nontrivial.

Accelerant components (artifact descriptions)
1) Risk-slicing canvas (one page) — sections:
   - Service surface & user impact categories (API, UI, batch, infra)
   - Failure modes and customer-facing symptoms mapped to SLO categories (latency, availability, correctness)
   - Signal priority (P1/P2/P3) with concrete metrics to collect in 48h after launch
   - Quick mitigations (auto-fallback, feature-flag kill-switch, capacity burst)
   - Escalation path and time-to-reach (TTR) targets

2) Ownership matrix (table) — rows by lifecycle activity, cols by role:
   - Activities: triage, incident lead, postmortem owner, config changes, capacity ops, security review
   - Roles: feature-oncall, SRE-duty, platform-support, infra-ops, security-contact

3) Quick-runbook flip (3-5 steps) — top-line runbook for first responders:
   - How to detect (playback of exact queries/dashboards)
   - Initial containment steps (kill-switch, redirect, degrade gracefully)
   - Communication script (what to post to Slack/email to stakeholders)
   - When to page who (thresholds)

Proposed 30/60/90 accelerant timeline (template to re-use)
- Day 0 (handoff meeting): Present risk-slicing canvas, ownership matrix; agree on immediate telemetry and a canary experiment.
- Day 1–7: Install primary dashboards, wire alerting to SRE rotation, smoke canary running at 1% traffic.
- Day 8–30: Expand canary to 10–25% while exercising fallback; run two tabletop drills with SRE and feature team.
- Day 31–60: Full rollout with solidified runbook; collect SLA-experience metrics and refine SLO thresholds if noisy.
- Day 61–90: Stability milestone review; confirm long-term monitoring, cost/scale tuning, and finalize SLO ownership for continuous improvement.

Decision anchors (examples to include in the handoff)
- Availability SLO example: 99.5% over a 30-day window for core read path. If breach probability > 2% during canary, require rollback or additional compensating controls.
- Latency threshold: 95th p50/p95 windows with specific query time budgets; page if sustained p95 > target for 5 minutes.
- Error budget policy: immediate freeze on feature pushes downstream if error budget burn rate > 4x for 1 hour.

Operational integrations (practical checklist)
- Dashboards: minimal set (success rate, latency p50/p95, traffic, infra CPU/memory, queue depth).
- Alerts: map to P1/P2 actions with runbook links.
- Telemetry hooks: add verbatim instrumentation calls and sample logs to the canvas.
- CICD: feature flag gating for canary rollouts and fast rollback play.
- Cost guard: expected cost delta and a fallback to limited capacity if cost spike > 20%/day.

Risk slicing examples (toy scenarios)
- Scenario A: New embeddings cache service (medium-risk) — high QPS, non-customer-visible recompute; risk slice: cache invalidation, memory leak, eviction storms. Mitigations: circuit-breaker, OOM alerts, progressive rollout.
- Scenario B: Shared routing layer change (high-risk) — customer-visible latency/availability; risk slice: routing table misconfiguration, hot-sharding. Mitigations: canary by region, read-only fallback, quick-config rollback path.

Meetings & collaboration rhythm
- Handoff kickoff (60 min): feature + SRE + platform — walk canvas and ownership matrix.
- Weekly 30-min check-ins during the first 30 days: quick health readout and action items.
- Post-30 day retro: decide on SLO tuning, long-term logging/observability needs.

Escalation and gating rules (proposal)
- Gating criteria to move from canary -> ramp -> full: must have at least 3d of stable canary metrics, runbook validated by SRE, and a rollback path confirmed.
- If any P1 incident occurs during canary, freeze rollout and perform a triage within 4 hours.

Owner/roles (proposed defaults)
- Handoff owner: feature/product engineering lead (responsible for canvas completeness).
- Operational steward: SRE assigned to the service for first 90 days.
- Platform contact: platform-engineering for rollout tooling and ops automation.
- Compliance reviewer: security representative for gated features.

Open questions / decisions needed
- What is the minimal telemetry set we will enforce (canonical metric names)? ACTION: platform to publish the minimal schema by 2026-12-01.
- Should we require an SLO sign-off from an SRE before moving to 25% traffic? (pros/cons listed below)
- Can the accelerant be integrated into the existing rollout checklist in Console? Who owns the UI bits?

Short-term next steps (owners & rough ETA)
- Publish a one-page risk-slicing canvas template — platform-engineering (Nora) — ETA 2026-11-25.
- Build a Dashboard seed in Grafana/Console for the template (Liam) — ETA 2026-12-08.
- Draft minimal-runbook flip template and a Slack incident script (Ava) — ETA 2026-12-01.
- Pilot with 2 teams (embeddings-cache and routing-layer) and capture lessons (Ravi & Samira) — start 2027-01-10.

Notes to self / rough ideas (scratchpad)
- Keep canvas printable and under one page; if it grows -> fail.
- Consider a small 'accelerant' badge that product teams can request to indicate readiness for SRE pairing.
- Explore small automations: template-to-dashboard one-click, auto-create runbook stub when a ticket references the canvas ID.

Appendix: Example minimal telemetry schema (proposal)
- success_rate: "service.<name>.success_rate"
- latency_ms: "service.<name>.latency.p95_ms"
- traffic_rps: "service.<name>.requests_per_second"
- infra_cpu_percent: "host.<name>.cpu_pct"
- error_budget_remaining_pct: derived metric

If you want this converted into a short Confluence how-to and a two-slide kickoff deck, I can draft both as next deliverables.
